title: The intergenerational clock: How advanced parental age shapes offspring biological aging, longevity and neurodegenerative risk
title_zh: 代际时钟：先辈高龄如何影响子代生物衰老、寿命与神经退行性疾病风险
abstract: BACKGROUND: As delayed parenthood becomes a global demographic norm, understanding the biological consequences of advanced parental age or APrA (≥35 years in mothers; ≥40 years in fathers) is a critical geroscience priority. This shift represents a significant public health challenge, as parental senescence dictates implications far beyond immediate fertility. APrA is a key determinant of offspring healthspan, linked to increased risks of congenital anomalies, premature mortality, neurodevelopmental and metabolic dysfunction, as well as neurodegenerative diseases. This inherited biological legacy supports an "intergenerational clock" linking reproductive timing to the aging trajectories of subsequent generations. SCOPE: This review synthesizes molecular mechanisms connecting parental senescence to reproductive success and offspring longevity. It examines the divergence between maternal factors, such as declining oocyte quality, and paternal factors, including sperm DNA fragmentation. Crucially, it integrates cross-species evidence ranging from Drosophila and mammalian models to human cohorts demonstrating how APrA progeny exhibit distinct behavioral phenotypes, including social deficits and anxiety, alongside compromised metabolic vitality. MAJOR CONCLUSIONS: Age-related modifications in DNA methylation, histone profiles, and non-coding RNAs serve as primary mediators, influencing gene regulation during early embryogenesis. These epigenetic processes interact with parental lifestyle and environment to alter germ cell programming. Propagated through intergenerational inheritance, these signatures increase susceptibility to neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. Ultimately, this reframes aging as a continuous intergenerational process rather than an isolated individual trajectory. GENERAL SIGNIFICANCE: Bridging reproductive biology and geroscience, this framework decodes how parental age shapes offspring biological legacy, essential for refining reproductive counseling and informing public health strategies.
abstract_zh: 背景：随着晚婚晚育成为全球人口趋势，了解先辈高龄（母亲≥35岁；父亲≥40岁）对生物学的影响已成为老龄科学的关键优先课题。这一转变构成了重大的公共卫生挑战，因为先辈衰老的影响远超即时生育。先辈高龄是子代健康寿命的重要决定因素，关联着先天异常、早期死亡、神经发育和代谢功能障碍以及神经退行性疾病风险的增加。这一遗传的生物学遗产支持了“代际时钟”概念，将生殖时机与后代衰老轨迹相连。范围：本综述综合了连接先辈衰老与生殖成功及子代寿命的分子机制。它考察了母体因素（如卵子质量下降）与父体因素（如精子DNA碎片化）的差异。关键的是，它整合了从果蝇、哺乳动物模型到人类队列的跨物种证据，展示了先辈高龄后代表现出独特的行为表型，包括社会缺陷和焦虑，以及代谢活力受损。主要结论：DNA甲基化、组蛋白谱和非编码RNA的年龄相关改变是主要介导因素，影响胚胎早期的基因调控。这些表观遗传过程与先辈的生活方式和环境相互作用，改变生殖细胞的编程。通过代际遗传传递，这些标记增加了神经精神和神经退行性疾病的易感性。最终，这重新将衰老视为连续的代际过程，而非孤立的个体轨迹。总体意义：通过桥接生殖生物学与老龄科学，本框架解码了先辈年龄如何塑造子代的生物学遗产，对完善生殖咨询和制定公共卫生策略至关重要。
